title: Appliance Rebates in Toronto 2026: Up to $200 Per Appliance
desc: Toronto appliance rebates for 2026: $25 to $200 under Home Renovation Savings for ENERGY STAR Most Efficient replacements, with Toronto Hydro as your distributor.
lead: Toronto has 1,160,895 households and 47% of them live in buildings of five or more storeys, where the in-suite appliances often belong to the building. The $25 to $200 rebates go to whoever buys the replacement.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for new appliances in Toronto
cards_intro: We re-read the program's appliance page on October 4, 2026. The rebates are province-wide, so the amounts are the same in every city, and the rules about what you replace and which model you buy are what decide a claim.

cards.title: Heat pump clothes dryer
cards.note: The largest of the six appliance rebates, for a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient heat pump dryer replacing an electric dryer.

cards.title: Induction cooktop or range
cards.note: For a new induction cooktop or range on the program's product list, replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Washing machine
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient washer on the program list.

cards.title: Fridge
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient refrigerator replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Freezer
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient freezer on the list.

cards.title: Dishwasher
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient dishwasher on the list.

cards.title: Who can claim
cards.note: A residential customer on the Ontario grid with an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. Cornwall Electric customers are excluded.

cards.title: Free route
cards.note: Income-qualified households can get energy-efficient fridges and freezers at no charge, along with other upgrades.

after_cards: The appliance page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: Towers, condos and who owns the fridge

With 47% of Toronto households in tall buildings and 48% renting, the first question is who owns the appliance. Rental suites often come with a fridge and range the landlord replaces. A condo owner who buys a new washer for their own unit is the person the rebate pays, subject to the program confirming condos, which its page does not address.

The rebate asks for a residential customer on the Ontario grid, which in most of the city means a Toronto Hydro account. Cornwall Electric customers are the only ones the page excludes by name. If your power is included in your rent, speak to the landlord about who claims, and whether they will.

Unlike the thermostat rebate, the appliance page lists no home type. It asks for a residential customer on the Ontario grid. It does not address condos or apartments directly, so a Toronto condo owner or tenant should confirm with the program. 48% of Toronto households rent, and a tenant should ask the landlord before swapping a fridge or range that came with the unit.
Most Efficient, not just ENERGY STAR

The rebate is for ENERGY STAR Most Efficient models, which the page describes as going beyond standard ENERGY STAR requirements. A fridge with the ordinary ENERGY STAR mark may not qualify. Each appliance has its own product list linked from the program page, so find the model number there before you pay, whether you buy in Toronto or online.
Fridges and freezers at no cost

The Energy Affordability Program lists energy-efficient refrigerators and freezers among the items that comprehensive support can provide, along with LED bulbs, dehumidifiers and window air conditioners. It does not list washers or dryers, and its saving kits include no major appliances. Income limits run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four, and Toronto postal codes are among those it covers. Call 1-844-770-3148 to ask.

The page states no limit per household and no end date. That does not mean unlimited funding, and the program can change. If you plan to replace a washer and a dryer, or a fridge and a freezer, get them on the program's lists first and keep every receipt, since each claim is separate and has its own 60-day window.
claim_steps: Check that the appliance you are replacing is electric and that you are on the Ontario grid.
Find a new model on the program's ENERGY STAR Most Efficient list for that appliance.
Buy it new from any retailer and keep the receipt.
Upload the receipt on the program page within 60 days of purchase.
If your household income is under the limits, call 1-844-770-3148 about free fridges and freezers first.
faq: Can a Toronto condo owner claim an appliance rebate?
The page lists no home type but does not mention condos. Ask the program before buying.
Is the Toronto HELP loan a rebate for appliances?
No. It is a loan for home energy improvements, and we did not find appliances listed there.
The heat pump clothes dryer, at $200.
The page does not say owners only. The landlord should agree to any swap.
